Does anyone know if GM has fixed their overheating problems with the C7?

At first I thought this happened at very high elevation like 11,000 feet but it turns out he was only at ~ 5,000'. My guess is that its a combination of things: high temperatures, hill climbing, heavy engine loads, thin air, and a license plate blocking off some of the airflow to the radiator. Maybe the only part of the radiator that was exposed was the part that the a/c condenser overlaps? Maybe there wasn't quite enough water in the coolant mix. Or there's something funky about the dry sump oiling that didn't quite compensate fully for the g-loading of taking sharp turns.

Of course, Chevrolet's customary habit of underengineering the product for extreme duty comes to mind as well. I've had similar problems while towing a trailer through high elevations in a GMC sport ute in the past. In my experience, engine load rather than high rpm seemed to correlate with heat buildup. Even though I never overheated I did find the engine ran hot. Turning up the heat and turning up the fan to help purge some of the heat helped, but choosing a higher gear never did anything for me.

As an aside, this is also a good reason to use synthetic oil or straight 30 weight oil as it it will be more shear stable at high temperatures.
